evidence.positive: Built the four-figure-ceiling scenario against the running app on demo-demo: created a 150 kg adult with no derivable ideal body weight (gender patched to non-binary, so LASTCommon.getTypedWeight doses on actual weight), a case, and one prior 10 mg nerve-block administration of Lidocaine-EPINEPHrine 2% via POST /api/admin/bolus. Selecting m-lidocaine-epinephrine-2-10 through POST /api/cds/medication-selection/{pmrn}/{caseId} as loopuser returned w-last-local-anesthetic-max-dose with needsAction=true, error=null. The details carry exactly the ticket's collision: NERVE_BLOCK_REMAINING_ALLOWED_DOSE = "1,039.5" (display string, comma present) alongside NERVE_BLOCK_REMAINING_ALLOWED_DOSE_AMOUNT_MG = 1039.5 (numeric). Both read sites behaved correctly on the numeric value: the rendered prompt quoted the remaining dose, "Max dose is 1,039 mg (=51 mL), adjusted for: ..." (NERVE_BLOCK_REMAINING_DOSE), not the 1,050 mg ceiling, and the citation resolved to r-last-local-anesthetic-concentration, the non-exhausted variant.
evidence.negative: Inverse case on the same patient and case: added a second prior administration of 1200 mg to exhaust the allowance, then re-selected the same medication. NERVE_BLOCK_REMAINING_ALLOWED_DOSE_AMOUNT_MG dropped to 0 and the guidance flipped in both places it is read - the prompt switched from the remaining dose to the ceiling, "Max dose is 1,050 mg (=52 mL), adjusted for: ..." (NERVE_BLOCK_MAX_DOSE), and the citation switched to r-last-local-anesthetic-concentration-max. So the numeric detail is genuinely driving both branches rather than the fix having pinned either one to a constant. Deleting the 1200 mg row and re-selecting returned the response to the four-figure remaining-dose form, confirming the flip was caused by the data and not by state drift.
evidence.red_check: Ran the pre-fix code in the container. Took the parent of the fix commit (git show e4b6da937^ of AbstractLocalAnestheticWarningOrInfoRule.java - the file is otherwise byte-identical to HEAD, so this isolates the two Double.parseDouble sites), replaced @Slf4j with an explicit org.slf4j.Logger since lombok is not on the runtime classpath, compiled it inside the container with javac against /app/jib-classpath-file, backed up the two shipped classes to /tmp/backup, copied the pre-fix classes into /app/classes and restarted the container. Re-running the identical positive request turned it red: the warning rule vanished from the response entirely (results contained only i-last-local-anesthetic), and the application log recorded 'Error processing rule: w-last-local-anesthetic-max-dose' followed by 'java.lang.NumberFormatException: For input string: "1,039.5"' at AbstractLocalAnestheticWarningOrInfoRule.getMatchingCitationDefinitions(...:461) -> getRouteBasedCitations(...:394) -> createPrompt(...:328) -> evaluate(...:81). That is precisely the ticket's symptom - the rule aborts and no guidance surfaces. Reverted: restored the backed-up classes and restarted; md5sums match the shipped originals exactly (ff2f18f6f252ee9112d733be49c76649 for the class, 4419f40948eb5f321a142f5cea73c4f6 for the $1 inner class), the positive case is green again, and the exception string appears exactly once in the whole container log - only inside the red-check window.

caveats: The four-figure ceiling was reached with a 150 kg patient whose ideal body weight is underivable (non-binary gender), so dosing falls back to actual weight; the ticket's own reachability path is Mayo's m-chloroprocaine-2-epinephrine at 14 mg/kg, which I could not exercise because that medication has no available routes in this instance's mayo-mayo data and no rule fires for it. The defective code path is identical either way - both arrive as a REMAINING_ALLOWED_DOSE string >= 1000.

Only the NERVE_BLOCK route was exercised. Epidural/spinal/intrathecal/topical map to the INFO rule, which the ticket correctly says never reads the dose - confirmed incidentally, since the INFO rule survived the pre-fix red check while the warning rule died.

The ticket's 'also worth checking' on w-acetaminophen-max-dose was inspected but not exercised at runtime: AbstractMaxDoseWarningRule writes REMAINING_ALLOWED_DOSE for display only and separately writes the numeric REMAINING_ALLOWED_DOSE_AMOUNT_MG for compliance, and a repo-wide search found no remaining site that parses the display string back to a number. No action appears needed there, but that conclusion is from reading, not from running it.
Locale is fixed to the container default in this instance, so the locale-dependence of the grouping separator (a comma here, a period or space elsewhere) was not varied.

automation.assessment: The fix already ships LocalAnestheticHighRemainingDoseTest, which is genuinely good: it pins the four-figure precondition explicitly (asserts REMAINING_ALLOWED_DOSE_AMOUNT_MG >= 1000 before asserting anything else, so the scenario cannot silently stop covering the bug if the mg/kg constant moves) and asserts which of the two values the rendered prompt quotes, in both directions. That covers the warning rule's prompt-text read at the unit level. Two things it does not cover: the citation-selection read, which is the site that actually threw in the red check here and is reached even with no prior administrations, and the end-to-end selection response.
proposed_tests: Unit (extend LocalAnestheticHighRemainingDoseTest): with a four-figure remaining dose and NO prior administrations, assert the warning rule still returns citations and that the chosen citation is the non-max variant - this pins getMatchingCitationDefinitions, the read that threw pre-fix, on the path the existing tests skip.

Unit (same class): with the allowance exhausted at a four-figure ceiling, assert the citation is the -max variant, so the citation read is pinned in both directions the way the prompt read already is.

qa-suite supplemental e2e (new LAST spec): stage a patient whose dosing weight puts a local anesthetic ceiling over 1000 mg, POST the medication selection, and assert the response contains w-last-local-anesthetic-max-dose with a prompt quoting the remaining dose - a regression guard at the API boundary, where the pre-fix build returned a 200 with the rule silently missing.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A local anesthetic selection with a four-figure remaining allowance (1,039.5 mg) produced the max-dose warning with guidance quoting the remaining dose.
Negative: Exhausting the allowance flipped the same guidance to the ceiling and to the max-dose citation, confirming the numeric value drives both branches.
Red check: Compiling the pre-fix class into the running container made the warning rule disappear with NumberFormatException for input string 1,039.5; the shipped class was restored and the positive case went green again.

Automation: Existing unit coverage pins the prompt-text read well; proposed additions cover the citation-selection read and an end-to-end selection guard.
